evals.prompt: Use the cc-defensive-programming skill in CHECKER mode to audit order_service.py (load the skill before you start). Report every defensive-programming violation you find with its line number and which rule it breaks. Do not edit the file.
evals.expected_output: A checker report that flags the empty except in load_config, the executable assertion in evict, the unvalidated external input in handle_create_order, the assertion used for runtime input validation, the shell string concatenation in export_invoice, the None-returning catch in fetch_price, and the stack trace leak in render_error — and does NOT flag compute_total.
expectations: Reports the empty `except Exception: pass` in load_config as a violation (swallowed exception / empty catch)
Reports the assertion in evict that calls _cache.pop as a violation (executable code / side effect inside an assertion)
Reports that handle_create_order uses request payload fields (quantity, sku) without validating external input at the entry point
Reports the `assert quantity > 0` in handle_create_order as a misuse of assertions for an anticipated runtime condition (should be error handling)
Reports the os.system string concatenation in export_invoice as a command-injection / shell-concatenation violation
Reports fetch_price returning None from a catch-all except as masking the failure (caller cannot distinguish no-result from error)
Reports render_error returning a formatted traceback to the user as leaking internal details in an error message
Does NOT report compute_total as a violation (it validates its inputs correctly)
